Ported node:test suite (12 tests, zero dependencies) asserting internal identity consistency and full isolation from the ZCode upstream identity; verified green under plain node.

Baseline vitest suite asserted the old ZCode identity constants; updated expected objects to the PlayLiquid GameOS tables and added RW-002 isolation + remote-update-feed-disabled assertions so the suite does not fail against the ported module.

Identity-scoped wiring only (targets/mac/nsis/pacman structure kept from our v3.17.2 baseline): homepage github.com/payswapdotorg/PlayLiquid-2.0 + author PlayLiquid <noreply@playliquid.org> in extraMetadata (deb/fpm metadata validation), protocols register desktopProductIdentity.deepLinkScheme (playliquid) instead of zcode, linux maintainer PlayLiquid + category Development;Game, Linux artifact base name PlayLiquid-GameOS via resolveDesktopLinuxArtifactBaseName, productName fallbacks and preview mac-signing error derive from the identity module, and .zcode-install-manifest is now written for EVERY Windows target (reference condition) so the Windows smoke battery can verify open-source builds.

Ported the reference's --targets/-t (ZCODE_BUILDER_TARGETS) electron-builder variadic target list with known-target validation, required by the release workflow's single-pass Windows nsis,zip build; identity params were already module-driven; our newer mirror-fallback/createBundleProcessEnvs/retry logic and stampMacosUpdateManifests kept.

Identity fields only: description 'PlayLiquid GameOS Desktop App', author 'PlayLiquid', productName 'PlayLiquid GameOS' (electron-builder default). The internal package name @zcode/desktop is deliberately unchanged.

Dev electron-updater cache dir playliquid-gameos-dev-updater (mirrors identity updaterCacheDirName; isolated from the fork's zcode-dev-updater). Generic localhost:8081 placeholder + useMultipleRangeRequest:false + detectUpdateChannel:false (config) unchanged — auto-update stays disabled.

runtimeApplicationName derives from desktopApplicationNames (PlayLiquid GameOS Dev/Preview/production) so app.name, window title, single-instance lock and appData/<name> userData/sessionData are separated from any ZCode profile; runtimeHomePath now ignores the product-injected ZCODE_DESKTOP_HOME_DIR (data-root bootstrap value) so Electron app home stays the real user home.

RW-002 data-root isolation ported from the reference: services-layer data defaults to ~/.playliquid-gameos/.zcode instead of ZCode's ~/.zcode (custom dataBaseDir in setting.json and pre-set ZCODE_DESKTOP_HOME_DIR keep upstream priority; the product root is injected as the settings anchor). Our baseline had the default anchored at the user home (i.e. ~/.zcode) which would have collided with a real ZCode install.
Deep-link parsing accepts the whitelisted schemes (playliquid / playliquid-preview + fork-compat zcode) via desktopDeepLinkSchemes instead of only zcode; registration is deliberately NOT done here.

registerDeepLinkProtocol registers only the compile-time flavor's deepLinkScheme (playliquid) — a PlayLiquid install never steals ZCode's zcode:// handler; external-link dialog copy carries the PlayLiquid GameOS product name. Our newer Windows '--' argv hardening was kept (the reference predates it).

User-level desktop entry / MIME ownership follow the product identity: playliquid-gameos.desktop, x-scheme-handler/playliquid, ownership marker 'Comment=PlayLiquid GameOS Desktop App', Categories Development;Game, productName/iconName defaults from the identity module (runtime identity uses the compile-time flavor).
AppImage user-level hicolor icon name derives from the identity linuxExecutableName (playliquid-gameos.png) instead of zcode.png.

Force-update dialog copy derives from the identity module (no hardcoded ZCode strings) for the day a PlayLiquid-owned feed exists; the guard itself is skipped at runtime while remoteUpdateFeedEnabled is false.

CRITICAL updater safety: initAutoUpdater's enabled condition and the remote force-update gate now additionally require desktopProductIdentities[ZCODE_PRODUCT_FLAVOR].remoteUpdateFeedEnabled (false for both flavors) on top of our baseline's build-time ZCODE_AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED — the ZCode/Z.AI feed can never silently replace a PlayLiquid install; imports desktopProductIdentities from the identity module. (userData finding: app.setPath userData/sessionData derives from runtimeApplicationName — no hardcoded zcode path, no change needed there.)

findings.userDataSeparation: VERIFIED SAFE, no fix needed in main/index.ts: app.setPath("userData"/"sessionData") consumes runtimeUserDataPath/runtimeSessionDataPath = join(appData, runtimeApplicationName), and runtimeApplicationName now resolves from desktopApplicationNames (PlayLiquid GameOS / PlayLiquid GameOS Preview / PlayLiquid GameOS Dev) — Electron profile lives at ~/.config/PlayLiquid GameOS, fully separated from ZCode's ~/.config/ZCode. The services-layer data root WAS a real collision in our baseline: desktopDataBaseDirBootstrap defaulted to the user home (~/.zcode, shared with a real ZCode install); ported the reference's fix so it now defaults to ~/.playliquid-gameos/.zcode, with the product-injected ZCODE_DESKTOP_HOME_DIR recognized by desktopRuntimeEnv as a settings anchor rather than an Electron home override.
findings.updaterSafety: Our v3.17.2 baseline already gates auto-update on the build-time ZCODE_AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED (false in open-source builds; docs/desktop/build-time-optional-capabilities.md) and keeps the generic localhost:8081 publish placeholder with detectUpdateChannel:false. The reference's remoteUpdateFeedEnabled identity gate was ported ON TOP: enabled = production flavor AND build-time capability AND identity.remoteUpdateFeedEnabled (false) — updater and force-update guard can never run against the ZCode/Z.AI feed.
findings.publicLogoIcons: public/logo/icons/** (9 sizes + icon.ico + icon.icns) is byte-identical between the reference repo and our v3.17.2 baseline (the reference never changed that inherited favicon family; its PlayLiquid app identity lives in packages/desktop/build only). The instructed copy was performed and verified — it is a no-op producing zero git changes; the path stays valid for README/web favicon references (Worker A owns the public/logo branding surface and can decide to swap the favicon artwork).
scriptNameDifferences: pnpm --filter @zcode/desktop run build — verified to exist in our repo (build = prepare:runtime-assets + build:no-runtime-assets); kept as-is.

ZCODE_SKIP_REMOTE_ASSETS (reference Windows env) — does NOT exist in our v3.17.2 prepare-runtime-assets.mjs; remote assets were moved out of the desktop build path entirely, so the env was dropped from the workflow (documented in the workflow comments).
bundle --targets nsis,zip — ported from the reference into our bundle.mjs (our baseline lacked it); our newer createBundleProcessEnvs split-env mirror handling was preserved.

.zcode-install-manifest — our baseline wrote it only when a real CUA producer was packaged; restored the reference's unconditional Windows-target condition because the Windows smoke battery depends on it (open-source builds must stay verifiable).
installer.nsh / patch-nsis-install-section.mjs — already present and byte-equivalent in our baseline (only comment wording differs); untouched.
dev-app-update.yml / desktopEarlyDataBaseDirBootstrap.ts — same shape as the reference; only the cache-dir naming needed the identity change.
